evidence: The only capacitors C1/C2 sit crammed in a right-edge column overlapping L1/L2, several cm from the +5V_RELAY coil pins they serve and not immediately adjacent to any power pin (no ICs exist to decouple).

Each channel reads top-to-bottom in signal order — driver cluster (D/R/Q plus flyback diode) above the relay coil pads, relay contacts below, screw terminal at the bottom edge — repeated identically for all four channels with no doubling back.

For every channel the relay NO/COM/NC contact pads land left-to-right in the same order as the terminal pins directly below (e.g. K1 NO x~196 -> J1 NO x~199, COM x~253 -> x~246, NC x~311 -> x~296), so straight pad-to-pad lines are near-vertical and never cross.

The switched-contact band (relay NO/NC/COM pads plus screw terminals) occupies the bottom region separated from all coil-side logic parts by a clear empty gap spanned only by the relay bodies, with no logic component inside it — though no physical isolation slot is present.

No power-entry connector exists and the +5V filter parts L1/C1/L2/C2 are stacked in an arbitrary overlapping right-edge column with long ratsnest reaches to the relay coil rail, so no input -> filter -> load placement order is discernible.
